seoTitle: Use TradingView Paper Trading & Fix a Missing Panel
metaDescription: Learn how to enable TradingView Paper Trading, place buy and sell orders, set stop loss and take profit, and fix the panel when it's not visible.
intro: Practicing trades without risking real money is exactly what TradingView's Paper Trading is built for, but a lot of users run into trouble when the panel simply won't show up, or they're unsure how to set proper exits on a simulated order. This guide walks through the actual Paper Trading panel — the account settings, the order ticket, and the positions view — so you can place buy and sell trades, attach stop loss and take profit levels, and read your results the same way you would on a live account. It closes with the fix for the panel-not-visible issue, which is almost always a layout problem rather than an account problem.

steps.heading: Switch to the Paper Trading tab
steps.body: On any TradingView chart, the bottom-left panel has two tabs: Trade and Paper Trading. Paper Trading is the one you want for practice, since it runs entirely on simulated funds against live or near-live prices. If you don't see this tab at all, it usually means your current layout has the bottom panel collapsed or hidden rather than the feature being unavailable — more on that fix later in this guide.

steps.heading: Set up or reset your paper account
steps.body: Before placing your first trade, it's worth opening Account settings to configure the account the way you actually want to practice with. Here you can reset the account entirely, which wipes existing orders, history, and positions and resets the balance to a value you choose, and you can set separate leverage ratios for stocks, futures, forex, and crypto. This matters because the default leverage on a fresh paper account may not match what you'd realistically get on a live account for the instrument you're practicing, and testing a strategy at 50:1 forex leverage when your real broker offers 10:1 will teach you the wrong lessons.

image.caption: The Reset account dialog, where you set a starting balance and per-asset leverage before wiping an existing paper account clean.

steps.heading: Place a buy or sell order
steps.body: With the Paper Trading panel open, click a symbol on your watchlist to load it, then use the Buy and Sell buttons at the top of the order ticket to open a position in either direction. You can choose Market, Limit, or Stop order types depending on whether you want the trade to fill immediately or wait for price to reach a specific level, which is the same choice you'd make with real capital.

steps.heading: Attach a stop loss and take profit
steps.body: The order ticket has an Exits section where you turn on "Take profit, price" and set a stop loss price below it, both expressed either as a price or in ticks from your entry. TradingView validates these as you type — notice the warning that a stop loss order must sit below your entry price for a long position, which stops you from submitting an exit that wouldn't actually protect the trade. Order info below shows your margin usage and leverage in real time, so you can see exactly how much of your simulated balance a given trade size ties up before you commit to it.

image.caption: The order ticket with Take profit and Stop loss fields filled in below the Buy/Sell buttons, plus a live margin and leverage readout.

steps.heading: Track positions, orders, and results
steps.body: Once a trade is live, the bottom panel switches to showing it under Positions, with running Account Balance, Equity, Realized P&L, and Unrealized P&L figures updating as price moves. The Orders and Order History tabs log every fill and pending order, and Trading Journal keeps a timestamped record of activations and executions — useful for reviewing what actually happened after a session rather than relying on memory. This is where paper trading earns its keep: the numbers behave like a real account, so bad habits show up here before they cost anything.

image.caption: The Paper Trading panel after a trade fills, showing account balance, equity, open orders, and a timestamped trading journal entry.

steps.heading: Fix the panel when it's not visible
steps.body: If the Paper Trading tab has vanished entirely, the most common cause is that the bottom panel got collapsed by an accidental drag or a keyboard shortcut. Look for a thin bar at the very bottom of the chart window and click it to expand the panel back out. If that doesn't bring it back, right-click anywhere on the chart and check that no custom layout is hiding the toolbar, since a saved layout from a different session can carry panel visibility settings with it.

steps.heading: Reset your layout as a last resort
steps.body: When reopening the panel doesn't work, resetting the chart layout to TradingView's default almost always clears the underlying conflict. This won't touch your paper account, balance, or trade history — it only affects which panels and toolbars are shown — so it's a safe step to try before assuming something is actually broken. After the reset, the Paper Trading tab should be back in its usual spot at the bottom of the chart.

faq.question: Why is my TradingView Paper Trading panel not showing up?
faq.answer: This is almost always a layout issue — the bottom panel got collapsed or a saved layout is hiding it — and can usually be fixed by expanding the panel bar or resetting your layout to default.

faq.question: Can I set a stop loss on a Paper Trading order?
faq.answer: Yes. The order ticket's Exits section lets you set both a take profit and a stop loss, in price or in ticks, with TradingView validating that the stop sits on the correct side of your entry.

faq.question: Does Paper Trading use real market prices?
faq.answer: Yes, Paper Trading fills against live or near real-time market prices while simulating the trade with virtual funds instead of real money.

faq.question: Can I reset my paper trading balance?
faq.answer: Yes, from Account settings you can reset the account, which clears orders, history, and positions and lets you set a new starting balance and leverage for each asset class.

faq.question: Is Paper Trading free to use on TradingView?
faq.answer: Paper Trading access can depend on your account type, so check your specific plan for availability and any related feature limits.
